documents.title: Preconception Counseling — Obstetrics & Gynecology
documents.author: obstetrics and gynecology
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS & GYNECOLOGY
Preconception counseling, visit of 04/08/2022
Copy to primary care at the patient's request

Mr. Mercier was seen together with his partner, who is a patient of our practice, to talk about planning a pregnancy.

Relevant history: Two of his siblings have cystic fibrosis. He himself is well, with no history of lung, sinus or digestive problems and no findings on history or exam to suggest CF. He has never had CFTR testing, so whether he carries a variant is not known. His partner's family has no known history of CF.

Other history: bipolar I disorder and schizotypal personality disorder, followed by psychiatry. Medications lithium carbonate 300 mg twice daily and lamotrigine 100 mg daily. No known drug allergies. Never smoker; drinks rarely.

Counseling: We reviewed that CF is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern through variants in the CFTR gene, so a child is affected only when both parents pass on a variant. Having two affected siblings and being unaffected himself raises his own chance of being a carrier well above the general population, where about 1 in 25 people carry a variant. We discussed carrier screening for both partners before conception and what each result would mean, including options if both were found to be carriers. The couple will think about testing and let us know.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM

26M with bipolar I and schizotypal PD (psychiatry).

Interval: Two things he hadn't mentioned. (1) Last fall he had a manic episode and was admitted to a psychiatric unit at an outside hospital for about a week. Discharged on the same lithium and lamotrigine. He didn't think to tell us. We never received anything. (2) Last month he and his partner went to her OB for preconception counseling because two of his siblings have CF. He was told his carrier chance is higher than average and that they could both get carrier testing. They haven't decided yet.

Feels well now. Sleeping 7-8 h. Classes going ok. Continues therapy with the psychiatry group. Taking meds daily.

Meds: lithium 300 BID, lamotrigine 100 daily. NKDA.
Social: still with roommate; partner lives in her own place. Never smoker, alcohol rare.

Exam: well, calm, linear. Normal HEENT, thyroid, heart, lungs, abdomen. No tremor.
PHQ-9 4.

A/P
1. Bipolar I with an admission fall 2021 — euthymic today. Records request to the outside hospital for the discharge summary. Lithium labs were done in March, normal; CBC today.
2. Schizotypal PD — in therapy.
3. Family hx CF / preconception — reasonable to do carrier testing; OB is handling; asked them to send their note.
4. HM — up to date; flu and COVID in the fall.

1 yr.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 10/12/2022
Copy to PCP

CC: brought in by roommate for strange behavior.

HPI: 27-year-old man with bipolar I disorder on lithium and lamotrigine, and schizotypal personality disorder (diagnosed October 2020 per psychiatry records), brought in by his roommate. For three days he has hardly slept and has worked around the clock on what he calls an invention that will change the world. Roommate describes him as far more talkative than usual, skipping from one subject to the next. He has charged thousands of dollars of electronics online this week. He is convinced his professors are monitoring him through his laptop and phone in order to take his ideas. Roommate says something similar happened about a year ago and he ended up hospitalized.

Meds: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID, lamotrigine 100 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father bipolar I; mother major depressive disorder; maternal uncle with schizotypal traits, undiagnosed.
Social: EE graduate student. Never smoker. Alcohol 1-2 drinks/month.

Exam: medically well appearing. Talkative, distractible, persecutory content as above.

Labs: urine drug screen negative.

ED course / MDM: Presentation consistent with a manic episode with psychotic features in known bipolar I disorder; no evidence of intoxication. Psychiatry consulted in the ED. Patient agreed to voluntary admission.

Diagnosis: Bipolar I disorder, current episode manic, with psychotic features.
Disposition: admitted to inpatient psychiatry.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Outreach
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Received ED record from 10/12 showing admission to inpatient psych. Called pt. He was discharged Friday 10/21. Sounds calm, says he's sleeping again and is back on lithium and lamotrigine, same doses. Has a psychiatry appointment next week. No discharge summary here yet; asked him to bring his discharge paperwork. Scheduled with PCP 11/1.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital f/u.

Admitted 10/12-10/21 inpatient psych at outside hospital for mania with psychotic features (ED record reviewed; no discharge summary yet and he didn't bring paperwork). He says he was there about 9 days, "they got me sleeping," and he left on the same lithium and lamotrigine doses he came in on. Saw his psychiatrist yesterday. Back in the lab part time, his advisor knows he was out.

Today: tired, a little flat, embarrassed about the spending, which he is sorting out with his bank. Sleeping 8-9 h. No racing thoughts. He no longer thinks his professors were watching him, says it "made sense at the time." No SI.

Meds: lithium 300 BID, lamotrigine 100 daily. NKDA.

Exam: calm, cooperative, speech normal rate, linear. Mild flat affect. No tremor. Heart and lungs normal.
PHQ-9 8.

A/P
1. Bipolar I disorder, recent manic episode with psychotic features, now settled. Psychiatry following closely. Lithium level, BMP, TSH today.
2. Records — will request discharge summary again.
3. Flu and bivalent COVID today.

Portal with labs. Physical in the spring/fall as usual.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical.

Big news: daughter born in July. He and his partner live separately; he is with them most evenings and weekends. Because of the CF in his family, the baby's pediatrician sent CFTR testing — he says it came back normal on both copies (homozygous normal, no variant found). Relieved. He never did his own carrier test.

Mood good. Sleep is "broken but that's the baby," averages 6-7 h. He knows sleep loss is a trigger and his partner covers some nights. Seeing psychiatry every 2-3 months, therapy less often now. No episodes since last fall.

Meds: lithium 300 BID, lamotrigine 100 daily. NKDA.
Social: PhD year 5, roommate same. Never smoker. Alcohol rare.

Exam: well. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No tremor. Mood euthymic.
PHQ-9 5.

A/P
- Bipolar I, euthymic — labs today, to psychiatry. Talked about protecting sleep.
- Schizotypal PD — stable.
- Family history: daughter's CFTR testing normal, noted.
- Flu and updated COVID today.

Next year.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lithium 0.6, kidneys, thyroid, calcium and blood counts all normal. Faxed to psychiatry at the new number. Congratulations again on your daughter.
